subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and a goal continuation driver as core runtime features now, and should the paired implementation land as one branch or be split?
rationale: The request changes core agent interaction semantics, gateway/protocol surfaces, channel delivery, Control UI behavior, and unattended goal continuation, so automation cannot safely choose the release shape or ownership boundary.

options.title: Stage the paired implementation
options.body: Keep this hub open and require focused review/proof for question pipeline, plan mode, and goal-driver groups before landing each part.

options.title: Sponsor the full branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the review and rollout cost for landing the broad paired PR after proof and CI are adequate.

options.title: Defer or narrow the roadmap
options.body: Maintainers can keep only the smaller already-supported primitives and ask for a narrower core API or plugin-facing design before more work lands.

recommendation.title: Stage the paired implementation
recommendation.body: Keep this hub open and require focused review/proof for question pipeline, plan mode, and goal-driver groups before landing each part.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal across strict-agentic, update_plan, Codex user-input, and goal surfaces that define this product decision.
